text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Copies of a secret electronic data base, compiled by the criminal police, have been sold on the black market for 50,000 kroons.
- Police have arrested three men in connection with a recent explosion in Tallin which injured three women.
- The right-wing Pro Patria party called for political parties to discuss the Estonian-Russian border agreement at a round table meeting on November 15.
- Parliament's special anti-corruption commission, headed by Reform Party MP Feliks Undusk, will start its investigation into property deals made by the Tallin city government.
- Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari will pay a one-day visit to Tallinn tomorrow.
- During trilateral negotiations, the government and employers refused a trade union demand that the minimum wage be raised from 680 to 1200 kroons.
